notes: All six speedup pairs match the README. Metadata checked on github.com: no license (LICENSE, LICENSE.md, COPYING all 404), 1 star, not a fork, last commit 2025-10-08 (within 12 months, active). Small win against an under-specified baseline; worth recording as a shortcoming.

tier_reason: README square-size table and raw results/gemm.csv give kernel vs cublasSgemm (CUBLAS_PEDANTIC_MATH) times; benchmark code is public (gemm/bench_gemm.cu), scripts/build.ps1 states nvcc from CUDA 13.3 with -O3 --use_fast_math -std=c++17 -lineinfo --expt-relaxed-constexpr -arch=sm_120 (MSVC 2022 host /O2), and the GPU is an RTX 5080.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: nvcc from CUDA 13.3 via scripts/build.ps1 (the README's build path): -O3 --use_fast_math -std=c++17 -lineinfo --expt-relaxed-constexpr -arch=sm_120, host MSVC 2022 BuildTools /O2,/std:c++17,/EHsc; CMakeLists.txt alternative uses the same nvcc options with CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=native
corrections.claimed_speedup: Faster than cuBLAS FP32 (pedantic) on every square N from 32 to 256 measured: 8.1 us vs 16.5 us at 32^3 (2.02x), 9.5 vs 16.2 us at 64^3 (1.71x), 9.3 vs 16.2 us at 96^3 (1.75x), 10.9 vs 16.2 us at 128^3 (1.49x), 11.9 vs 16.9 us at 192^3 (1.42x), 13.6 vs 17.8 us at 256^3 (1.30x). Slower everywhere else measured: tall-skinny shapes 0.22x-0.93x (4096x64x4096 is 0.90x), and per results/gemm_tf32.csv the auto kernel is at 3.52 vs 11.46 TFLOP/s at 512^3 (0.31x) and 23.05 vs 36.79 TFLOP/s at 4096^3 (0.63x).
corrections.caveats: The win is cuBLAS's roughly 16 us per-call floor on tiny matrices, not arithmetic throughput; from 512^3 up and on every tall-skinny shape it is slower than cuBLAS FP32. The license was changed from MIT to a view-only 'all rights reserved' text in the second of three commits (same day, 2026-08-25), so the current code cannot be copied, used, or used in a benchmark publication. One GPU, one build, measured on Windows only; compiled with --use_fast_math; the README gives 15 warm-ups and about 150 ms of GPU work per measurement but no run counts or variance.

notes: Numbers match README and results/gemm.csv; the 4096^3 table units are TFLOP/s per results/gemm_tf32.csv. Metadata checked on github.com: LICENSE is all-rights-reserved source-available (usability reference is right), 0 stars, 3 commits, last 2026-08-25, not a fork.

tier_reason: README 'Results in short' and the LIBXSMM/KleidiAI/OpenBLAS table give geometric-mean GFLOPS vs Accelerate, OpenBLAS 0.3.34, Eigen, LIBXSMM and KleidiAI; benchmark code is public (bench/bench.cpp, bench/bench_ext.cpp, bench/bench_eigen.cpp, bench/bench_openblas.cpp, bench/run_all.sh), Makefile flags -std=c++17 -O3 -DNDEBUG -march=armv8.6-a+sme2+sme-f64f64, Apple clang 21 on macOS 27.0, Apple M4 Pro.

corrections.claimed_speedup: FP32 geomean 2777 vs 2363 GFLOPS for Accelerate on the paper's 24 column-major workloads at default threading (1.18x; 1.17x row-major); one thread, paper's 24 workloads: 1421 vs 1196 (1.19x column-major) and 1416 vs 1124 (1.26x row-major); squares 512-4096 one thread only 1.04x-1.06x; 1.25x row-major / 1.19x column-major vs Accelerate in the paper-comparison table (fp64 1.29x one thread); 3.70x faster than OpenBLAS 0.3.34 (row-major), 2.20x faster than LIBXSMM (column-major) and 1.67x faster than KleidiAI (one thread); Eigen master 1044 GFLOPS vs 2777 at default threading.
corrections.caveats: Reproduction of the paper arXiv:2512.21473 (MpGEMM, whose authors released no code), by a single author, measured on one shared machine (one-minute load 1.5-5.6 during final runs; minimum of five trials, which the README says is a few percent more favourable than the paper's mean) with an 8 P-core M4 Pro vs the paper's 10 P-core; at default threading it is slower than Accelerate (below 0.9x) on 10 of 484 grid shapes and below 64^3 (0.17x-0.9x); the win on squares 512-4096 on one thread is only 4-6%; the Accelerate version is not stated beyond macOS 27.0; the OpenBLAS 0.3.34 figure in the LIBXSMM/KleidiAI comparison is one Homebrew-build measurement that falls back to NEON at M=4096; OpenBLAS develop's own SME kernels reach 0.50x-0.78x of MTGEMM-A on one thread; macOS cannot pin the two worker threads to separate SME clusters; no-transpose GEMM only. The repo also carries an OpenBLAS port (branch sme2-gemm of the author's OpenBLAS fork, not yet submitted) and an Eigen SME GEMM backend developed from this code. Wave 8 leads.md already lists this repo as a candidate for the MpGEMM paper entry.
